sources.entry: WFGY - Open source framework for debugging LLM agents and RAG pipelines with a 16-mode ProblemMap and practical triage checklists.

summary.one_liner: WFGY is an open-source ecosystem whose flagship, WFGY 5.0 Polaris Protocol, is a staged rollout of protocol components, public evidence packages, and a Problem Map 3.0 troubleshooting gate for broken LLM and RAG workflows.
summary.what_it_does: The README is mostly a navigation page for the WFGY ecosystem rather than a documented software package. It describes Polaris Goal Compiler, a portable human-AI execution protocol meant to be pasted into an assistant, agent rule file, or workflow policy, aimed at compiling user goals before execution and verifying before unlocking downstream work. It publishes "Polaris Experiments" as evidence packages with raw outputs, parsed outputs, verdicts, token records, audits, and SHA256 hashes. For broken workflows it points to Problem Map 3.0 (Atlas Router TXT, Global Debug Card, Global Fix Map). It also lists WFGY 3.0 TXT packs with a SHA256 verification step, and WFGY 4.0 governance materials. The README does not show code, installable packages, or concrete API usage.
use_cases: writing agent rule files that prevent premature task completion
verifying integrity of a downloaded WFGY TXT pack
reviewing public evidence for AI experiments
how_to_run: Download the Polaris Goal Compiler text and paste it into an AI assistant or agent rule file to test it
Open Problem Map 3.0 (Atlas Router TXT, Global Debug Card, Global Fix Map) for a failing workflow
Download the WFGY 3.0 TXT pack, then verify its SHA256 against the value listed in the README
notable: Polaris Goal Compiler: a portable prompt-style protocol for human-AI task execution, released as a text component
Problem Map 3.0 troubleshooting atlas with a router TXT, debug card and fix map for RAG and agent failures
Public evidence packages with raw outputs, verdicts, token accounts and SHA256 integrity records
Staged, batch-by-batch release model in which deeper engine components are deferred
caveats: Deeper engine, runtime structures and reproduction materials are not yet released; the README says they will come in later batches
The README is largely a link hub with little concrete technical detail, code or install steps
Licensing is only stated as MIT in the footer; the FAQ says to check the repository for license terms
keywords: check if my rag is broken
